topics.title: Computational Imaging and Spectral Reconstruction

trustAssessment.basis: The source inventory is complete. Unresolved identities remain flagged, and topic evidence thresholds have not been assigned.

paragraphs: Spectral reconstruction estimates wavelength-dependent information from camera measurements. The inversion depends on calibration, illumination, sensor response and model assumptions. The research spans sparse recovery, neural networks and methods using a physical colour reference chart. Reconstructed channels carry the conditions of the method that produced them.

The Purdue study, repeated as NPL-1 and NPL-153, uses a specially designed spectral colour chart with a computational method. Its reported framework operates in the visible range. It does not establish unrestricted recovery of near-infrared information from any ordinary RGB photograph. For each approach, the research question is how accurately spectra transfer to new devices, lighting conditions, samples and acquisition settings.

topics.title: Optical Physiology and Tissue Imaging

trustAssessment.basis: The source inventory is complete. Unresolved identities remain flagged, and topic evidence thresholds have not been assigned.

paragraphs: Optical physiology studies connect image variation with quantities such as blood volume, perfusion and oxygenation. The source collection brings rPPG, tissue hyperspectral imaging, skin fluorescence and endoscopic reconstruction into one reading path. Each method retains its own hardware, tissue and reference measurement.

The endoscopy study at NPL-221 examines hyperspectral conversion and CycleGAN-generated narrowband images in an esophageal imaging setting. Its clinical context is distinct from a smartphone facial measurement. Oxytocin and baroreflex papers provide physiological context for potential optical associations; they do not, by themselves, establish gene-specific measurement from facial images. Validation needs paired reference assays and controls for motion, lighting, skin pigmentation and vascular state.

topics.title: Autofluorescence and Molecular Sensing

trustAssessment.basis: The source inventory is complete. Unresolved identities remain flagged, and topic evidence thresholds have not been assigned.

paragraphs: Autofluorescence describes light emitted by endogenous molecules after excitation. The cited work covers metabolic coenzymes, proteins, tissue fluorescence and image analysis. Interpretation depends on excitation and emission bands, optical depth, background signals and the mixture of fluorophores in the sample.

The bibliography also includes chemical probes, immunoassays and genetically encoded sensors. These methods need explicit labels for reagents, sample preparation, instrumentation and biological setting. A smartphone-linked assay and an unmodified phone camera observing intact skin are different experimental systems. Fractal descriptions and molecular geometry remain research frameworks to test against measured data.

trustAssessment.basis: The source inventory is complete. Unresolved identities remain flagged, and topic evidence thresholds have not been assigned.

paragraphs: SpectralSeq pairs hyperspectral autofluorescence microscopy and RNA sequencing from the same individual cells. The published study connects optical and morphological features with transcriptomic variation in the tested cell system. NPL-9b records the publication; NPL-9 and NPL-214 retain its HyperSeq preprint provenance.

This supplies an experimental route for studying relationships between optical phenotype and molecular state. The proposed extension to facial imaging and gene-specific inference remains a hypothesis. The next questions concern paired ground truth, cell and tissue specificity, confounding, repeatability and independent validation. TFBS, chromatin and protein-structure publications provide supporting molecular context, with their distinct methods and scales retained.

chapters.title: DOCK2, trauma and PTSD: DNA methylation and gene expression
overview: Universal Mind is investigating whether its interventions, developed around hypotheses concerning oxytocin receptor signalling, are associated with changes in DOCK2 gene expression or DNA methylation. DOCK2 is an exploratory biological outcome alongside symptoms, functioning and wellbeing. The aim is to test whether it can provide an early signal of intervention response.

DOCK2 means dedicator of cytokinesis 2. It is distinct from the DOC2 family. Published human studies connect DOCK2 with PTSD-associated methylation, with limited expression evidence and mixed replication. These observations motivate a longitudinal research question; they do not establish a beneficial direction of change or a validated surrogate for recovery.

Research purpose: intervention response, not initial diagnosis. The proposed chain from an intervention to OXTR-related biology, to DOCK2 change, to clinical benefit contains several untested links. Measuring each link separately keeps the hypothesis testable. Literature reviewed 21 November 2026; this is a targeted narrative evidence map, not a systematic review.

topics.title: Research purpose · intervention response and OXTR
topics.description: What excites us: the possibility of pairing lived improvement with repeatable molecular measurements, and of learning whether immune-related biology changes during recovery. Published psychotherapy studies demonstrate ways to examine molecular trajectories, while their positive and null findings help define a rigorous test.
paragraphs: EMDR has clinical efficacy evidence as a complete trauma-focused psychotherapy delivered by trained clinicians. Universal Mind’s experimental visual, auditory and other components require their own evaluation; using an EMDR-related component does not establish the efficacy of the full therapy or an OXTR mechanism.

Measure RNA expression and DNA methylation separately. RNA abundance measures gene output; methylation measures chemical marks at specified DNA sites. Neither directly measures oxytocin release, receptor activation or immune-protein function. Increased expression and increased methylation are not automatically beneficial.

A proposed longitudinal study pairs baseline, early, post-intervention and follow-up samples with validated symptom and functioning measures, a suitable comparison condition, and a prespecified analysis. Match tissue, collection time and laboratory methods; assess cell composition, medication, smoking, recent infection and other relevant confounders. Register candidate CpGs, expression endpoints, timing and multiple-testing correction before analysis.

An early molecular association becomes informative when it is reproducible, exceeds technical variation, differs meaningfully from the comparison condition and relates to later improvement. A DOCK2 change alone is not a success criterion. Clinical improvement without a DOCK2 change remains a meaningful outcome; a DOCK2 change without improvement remains an exploratory observation.

chapters.title: IL-6, mental health and inflammation: oxytocin and OXTR pathways
overview: IL-6 is associated with several mental-health conditions, especially depression, psychosis, bipolar disorder, PTSD and substance use disorders. The evidence varies by diagnosis, mood state, specimen and study design. It does not establish IL-6 as a universal cause of mental illness or prove that lowering it improves every condition.

This chapter retains the original 42-source OXTR analysis and adds 120 peer-reviewed publications: 117 directly relevant mental-health papers plus three contextual substance-exposure papers. Randomized trials lead the appraisal; positive, null and opposite-direction findings remain visible. Publication counts are not counts of independent experiments.

Oxytocin–OXTR anti-inflammatory mechanisms have strong support in selected cell models and substantial animal evidence. Human OXTR–IL-6 evidence is emerging, promising and mixed. Direct IL-6 receptor trials in depression and schizophrenia remain small, inconclusive or negative; a sustained clinical benefit through the proposed Universal Mind pathway is unestablished.

The systems-biology opportunity is a testable human hypothesis: does a defined intervention alter OXTR-related biology, IL-6 signalling and meaningful outcomes, and which links are actually demonstrated? Each link needs evidence. Universal One retrieves this same appraised literature, with source-specific access and limitations.

topics.title: In a dish: strong mechanisms, defined boundaries
topics.description: Human-derived cells provide direct mechanistic evidence, but results depend on cell type and experimental conditions.
paragraphs: The clearest early result is direct suppression of IL-6 release in selected macrophage and vascular-cell systems. Follow-up work places OXTR inside an inflammation-sensitive feedback loop: inflammatory activation can increase receptor availability, after which oxytocin can alter the response. This is biologically persuasive within those systems; it is not evidence that every human immune cell responds in the same way.

The negative donor-cell study is essential to the interpretation. A result in THP-1-derived macrophages does not automatically reproduce in freshly isolated monocytes or differently prepared macrophages. Receptor abundance, differentiation state, donor characteristics, challenge strength, pretreatment and sampling time can all matter. Independent replication across donors and laboratories is more informative than counting several outputs from one cell line as separate confirmations.

Oxytocin is not a universal suppressor of NF-κB or ERK. NF-κB helps induce OXTR in activated macrophages, while ERK participates in oxytocin signalling and fibroblast protection. In gestational tissues, oxytocin can instead promote inflammatory pathways associated with labour. The direction of a pathway response depends on the tissue and its physiological task.

Mechanistic confidence rises when a result survives selective receptor perturbation, a dose-response analysis and independent replication. A fall in IL6 messenger RNA alone remains several steps from lower secreted IL-6, reduced inflammatory injury and improved human health. The chapter keeps those measurements separate.

topics.title: Microglia and neuroinflammation
topics.description: Several preclinical routes converge on inflammatory regulation; they do not establish one universal signalling cascade.
paragraphs: Microglia provide complementary examples. One study found reduced ERK/p38 responses, another implicated eIF2α–ATF4 without comparable NF-κB/p38 changes at the measured times, and recent transcriptomics identified IL-17-linked expression patterns. These are model-specific mechanisms. They cannot be combined into a single proven linear sequence from OXTR to every inflammatory pathway.

The 2026 IL-6/COX-2 paper adds a useful molecular lead. Its key endpoint is gene expression in a mouse microglial line. IL-17 pathway enrichment describes a statistical pattern in the transcriptome; it does not demonstrate selective IL-17 inhibition, lower IL-6 protein in human blood, or clinical neuroprotection.

Animal work extends beyond molecular changes to myelination, connectivity, behaviour and memory. Those functional outcomes strengthen the preclinical rationale. Yet perinatal injury, acute LPS challenge and chronic human neurological disease differ in timing, immune state and drug exposure. Carbetocin and oxytocin also require separate pharmacological interpretation.

Peripheral and central measurements answer different questions. A blood cytokine result cannot by itself demonstrate altered microglial activity. Receptor antagonism adds evidence, but imperfect drug selectivity and the timing of administration remain relevant. A human study needs to state whether it is testing peripheral inflammation, symptoms, or a specifically measured central mechanism.

topics.title: Gut inflammation, immune cells and the mucus barrier
topics.description: Receptor deletion and cell-specific experiments provide some of the strongest causal evidence in animals.
paragraphs: The intestinal literature tests more than an association between oxytocin and a cytokine. Whole-body and cell-specific OXTR perturbations alter experimental colitis, providing evidence that the receptor participates in immune and barrier regulation. Macrophage and dendritic-cell studies connect signalling with inflammatory-cell states and tolerance.

A newer epithelial mechanism links OXTR to mucus maturation and fucosylation. A stronger barrier may reduce inflammatory exposure upstream of cytokine production. This complements direct immune-cell mechanisms and explains why measuring only circulating IL-6 can miss an important local response.

Human biopsy findings increase biological relevance but remain observational. Mouse colitis, cell transfer and receptor deletion do not establish an effective human oxytocin treatment for ulcerative colitis or cancer. Developmental consequences of whole-body knockout and the acute injury caused by DSS are material model limitations.

topics.title: Systemic inflammation and regulatory markers
topics.description: Lower inflammatory signalling and stronger regulatory responses can occur together, but each marker needs a biological context.
paragraphs: The obese-mouse study is useful because it separates tissue and blood endpoints: lower adipose IL6/TNF expression, lower circulating serum amyloid A and higher adiponectin occurred without parallel improvements in weight or glycaemia. Biomarker movement is therefore not interchangeable with broad clinical or metabolic improvement.

Periodontal and chronic-stress models extend the evidence to different tissues and immune settings. In the stress model, oxytocin-related pathways favoured regulatory immune features and suppressed some effector responses. Describing this as improved immune balance is more precise than asserting that oxytocin boosts all immunity.

IL-10 and IL-1 receptor antagonist can be informative regulatory markers. Adiponectin may be useful in metabolic questions. IL-4, IL-13 and TGF-β have context-dependent roles, including repair and potentially unwanted remodelling. No marker is a universal wellness score, and a larger regulatory-cytokine response can simply reflect a larger inflammatory challenge.

topics.title: Human experiments: emerging, promising and mixed
topics.description: There is direct human evidence, including an acute IL-6 signal, alongside important null and opposite-direction findings.
paragraphs: The 2008 endotoxin experiment is a proof-of-mechanism lead: intravenous oxytocin attenuated the acute inflammatory and stress response in ten healthy men. It is a small, highly controlled challenge study. It does not establish that intranasal oxytocin or a non-drug intervention lowers persistent IL-6 in a clinical population.

The wound studies make the human story more nuanced. In women, oxytocin combined with a positive couple interaction was linked to higher local wound IL-6 and lower IL-1β. That pattern can coexist with repair. Wound-fluid cytokines and resting blood cytokines answer different questions; labelling every IL-6 increase as harm or every decrease as benefit loses that distinction.

The later wound-healing publication analyses the same 80 couples. It adds a different outcome, not a second independent trial. Its combined-intervention signal weakened in sensitivity analysis, and it does not establish that IL-6 mediated healing. The source register links both papers to the same study family.

The autism datasets also resist a simple suppression model: selected cytokines increased after a particular intranasal formulation and dose. Plasma immune changes, social outcomes and central inflammation remain distinct endpoints. Together, the human studies support further testing of context-dependent immunomodulation; sustained clinical anti-inflammatory efficacy remains unestablished.

topics.title: New human findings and meaningful negative results
topics.description: Proteomics, baseline inflammation and epigenetics help refine the question; none supplies a validated OXTR–IL-6 treatment biomarker.
paragraphs: Acute plasma proteomics shows that intranasal oxytocin can be accompanied by broad biological changes. This is useful pharmacodynamic exploration, but pathway enrichment and differential proteins require independent, targeted validation before they become a clinical anti-inflammatory claim.

The obesity conference abstract supplies a relevant counterweight: inflammatory-proteome differences did not survive multiple-testing correction. Its preliminary publication format limits appraisal, yet the null finding belongs in the evidence map. It does not establish a reliable chronic anti-inflammatory effect, and nominal individual signals cannot override the corrected result.

Baseline inflammation may modify response in unexpected directions. In the psychiatric secondary analysis, symptom benefit was associated with lower baseline NLR. This is a response-moderation result, not demonstrated reduction of inflammation, and it cautions against assuming that the most inflamed group necessarily benefits most.

OXTR methylation provides a further human association, involving stress and TNF in older adults. A CpG-specific peripheral association is not receptor activation, does not imply the same effect in brain tissue, and cannot establish an intervention pathway. Methylation, expression, protein abundance and function need separate labels.

topics.title: Why IL-6 needs a deeper interpretation
topics.description: IL-6 has inflammatory, protective and repair-related functions. Its source, duration and receptor route matter.
paragraphs: An acute IL-6 response can recruit regulatory mediators. Human IL-6 infusion increased IL-10 and IL-1RA, illustrating why IL-6 is not simply a toxin to eliminate. Persistent elevation, acute exercise-related signalling and local wound repair are different biological situations. A study needs to define the situation it intends to change.

In classical signalling, IL-6 binds membrane IL-6 receptor and recruits gp130. In trans-signalling, IL-6 binds soluble IL-6 receptor and can stimulate gp130-expressing cells without their own membrane IL-6 receptor. The routes have different cellular reach; a classical-good/trans-bad label is an incomplete account of biology. Soluble gp130 can inhibit the trans-signalling complex in defined systems.

A phase 2 olamkicept trial illustrates that targeting this pathway can have clinical relevance in ulcerative colitis. It is evidence about a different drug. The studies assembled here do not demonstrate that oxytocin selectively blocks IL-6 trans-signalling. Measuring sIL-6R and sgp130 can add context, but concentrations alone cannot prove pathway inhibition.

A useful biomarker panel separates the primary question from supporting measurements. Preselect one main IL-6 endpoint if IL-6 is the biological focus; use regulatory cytokines and downstream markers to interpret it. Label this as a proposed research panel, not a validated diagnostic or treatment-response test.

biomarkers.interpretation: Specify blood or tissue, baseline or challenge response, timing and assay sensitivity. A lower value is not automatically beneficial in every setting.
Reflects transcription in the sampled cells. It is not interchangeable with secreted protein or circulating IL-6.
Measure alongside inflammatory burden. Values may decline when the provoking inflammatory response declines.
CRP integrates a downstream acute-phase response; TNF and IL-1β have distinct kinetics. These are not anti-inflammatory markers.
Adiponectin can support a metabolic mechanism; SAA is an inflammatory acute-phase marker. The oxytocin evidence here is principally preclinical.
Concentrations alone do not establish functional trans-signalling. Cell-response assays can test a specific pathway hypothesis.
Avoid a universally beneficial direction. Interpret with tissue remodelling, immune state and the study question.
Specify cell type, CpG site and assay. Expression or methylation is not receptor occupancy, activation or central target engagement.
Validate the complete analytical method. A concentration is not proof that the intervention acted through OXTR.
Cell composition can affect molecular assays. NLR is an indirect index and is not a substitute for IL-6.

topics.title: A testable research direction for Universal Mind
topics.description: The opportunity is a carefully specified human study of intervention response, with receptor-related mechanisms treated as hypotheses.
paragraphs: Universal Mind can investigate whether a defined intervention is associated with changes in IL-6, regulatory immune markers and wellbeing, and whether OXTR-related measures help explain those changes. Existing literature already connects oxytocin with human cytokine responses. The useful contribution is a new, well-controlled intervention–population–measurement combination; this review does not establish first-ever priority for the general relationship.

OXT and OXTR are different genes: OXT encodes the hormone precursor, while OXTR encodes its receptor. Exogenous oxytocin, a related receptor agonist, and a behavioural or sensory intervention are different exposures. For Universal Mind’s non-drug approaches, “developed around an OXTR-related hypothesis” is accurate until receptor mediation is demonstrated. Clinical improvement alone cannot establish that mechanism.

Proposed design: randomise participants to the defined intervention and a credible active comparison matched for time, attention, expectation and relevant social contact. Prespecify one primary biological endpoint, its collection window and its analysis. Keep a clinical or wellbeing endpoint distinct. Use blinded laboratory analysis and balance study groups across assay batches. Determine sample size from the expected variability and a scientifically meaningful effect; use an initial pilot to estimate feasibility and variance rather than claim definitive efficacy.

Choose between two different questions. An acute study tests a time course or prespecified area under the curve after a session or challenge. A longitudinal study tests a sustained change across weeks, ideally using repeated baseline and follow-up measurements. Combining both is possible, but their hypotheses and multiplicity plan need to remain explicit. Recent infection, vaccination, exercise, sleep, adiposity, medication, hormonal context and collection time can change inflammatory measurements.

For the primary assay, specify plasma or serum, sample processing, storage, lower limit of quantification and a plan for censored values. Saliva is a different matrix. Prespecify transformation or a suitable skewed-outcome model, intention-to-treat analysis, missing-data handling and correction for secondary cytokine comparisons. Record blood counts and cell composition when interpreting transcriptomic or methylation data. Baseline-inflammation subgroup analyses need prospective specification.

A practical exploratory panel can pair IL-6 with IL-10, IL-1RA, hs-CRP and selected inflammatory cytokines. Add sIL-6R/sgp130, receptor expression or site-specific methylation only when each answers a clear question. An ex vivo blood-cell experiment with an appropriate selective antagonist, viability controls and matched stimulation may test receptor dependence outside the participant; it does not prove the intervention engaged brain OXTR.

Oxytocin assays require special care. Extraction can remove interfering material but can also lose analyte; non-extracted assays require their own validation. Select a validated complete method and document specificity, recovery, dilution behaviour, precision and matrix effects. A plasma oxytocin change is an exploratory measure, not a direct readout of receptor activation.

The causal question has several links: intervention exposure, a receptor-related response, inflammatory change, and a meaningful human outcome. Correlated change across those links does not prove mediation. Temporal ordering, randomisation, prespecified mediation analysis and an independent receptor-function experiment can strengthen the inference. If wellbeing improves without IL-6 changing, that remains informative. If IL-6 changes without clinical benefit, it remains a biological result rather than demonstrated therapeutic success.

The positioning is therefore positive and testable: strong preclinical mechanisms justify focused human investigation; mixed human findings define the gap. Universal Mind can contribute by measuring that gap carefully and publishing beneficial, null and unexpected-direction results with equal clarity.

topics.title: Source appraisal and limits of this review
topics.description: A targeted narrative evidence map, expanded from the supplied Scholar collection and checked on 24 November 2026.
paragraphs: The supplied PDF contained 19 distinct scholarly sources after deduplication. This chapter retains all 19 and adds primary human experiments, negative studies, receptor-mechanism papers, assay research and official reference records. The resulting 42 sources include reviews, a thesis, a conference abstract, gene records and a withdrawn trial registration; 42 sources does not mean 42 independent experiments.

Searches covered oxytocin/OXTR with IL-6, inflammatory cytokines, microglia, macrophages, colitis, human randomised trials, endotoxin, wound healing, proteomics, methylation and assay validation. PubMed/Europe PMC, publisher pages, accessible full text, university repositories and ClinicalTrials.gov were checked. Source records state whether full text, an abstract or a registry was available. This is a deep narrative analysis, not a preregistered systematic review, exhaustive search or meta-analysis.

No pooled effect size is presented because populations, species, tissues, routes, doses, timing and outcomes differ substantially. Formal risk-of-bias and GRADE assessments were not performed. The overview uses qualitative judgments about mechanistic support and human translation; publication design icons are not certainty grades. Publication bias and selective reporting remain possible, particularly across small preclinical experiments.

Reviews help locate original studies but do not add independent experimental replication. The master’s thesis and later macrophage publication share a research lineage; full-text access was insufficient to resolve exact data overlap. The two couple studies explicitly share a trial family. These relationships are recorded so source volume does not inflate confidence.

Source checking also identified a gene-identity error in one supplied review. The chapter retains that paper for provenance, flags the error and uses official gene annotations for the hormone–receptor distinction. Claims about tissue-specific effects, negative results and human uncertainty are retained even when they complicate the therapeutic narrative.

topics.title: IL-6 across mental health: the evidence map
topics.description: A shared research pathway with diagnosis-specific limits.
paragraphs: IL-6 is a credible transdiagnostic research pathway, with repeated group-level associations across depression, psychosis, bipolar disorder, PTSD and substance use disorders. That does not establish IL-6 as the core cause of every mental illness, or as abnormal in every affected person. Anxiety and ADHD findings are less consistent. The most useful question is which phenotype, tissue, time course and signalling process is involved, and whether changing that process improves an outcome that matters to people.

This expansion contains 120 peer-reviewed publications: 117 directly relevant mental-health papers and three contextual substance-exposure papers. These are publications, not 120 independent experiments or 120 randomized trials. Reviews reuse primary studies, some reports share cohorts, and several analyses are secondary outcomes from trials. The original 42-source OXTR register remains alongside this expansion; its source types include material beyond peer-reviewed experiments. The combined chapter has 162 distinct source records.

The hierarchy begins with direct pathway intervention, followed by randomized interventions that measure IL-6, genetic and longitudinal studies, case-control comparisons, and mechanistic work. A treatment RCT can establish an intervention effect without proving that IL-6 mediated it. A meta-analysis can strengthen evidence for an association while inheriting confounding from the studies it pools. A genetic instrument can help test causality, but is not equivalent to a prescription or a short-term change in blood IL-6.

Childhood IL-6 preceded later depression and psychotic experiences in ALSPAC, but the estimate for diagnosed psychotic disorder was imprecise. Temporal ordering is useful evidence, not a complete causal demonstration. Similar cohort names across papers signal related evidence rather than new independent populations. No individual diagnostic threshold or reliable suicide-risk classifier is established by this evidence map.

topics.title: Depression: association is stronger than treatment proof
topics.description: Direct IL-6 receptor trials, adjunctive RCTs, symptoms and genetic evidence.
paragraphs: The most direct test in this set is the 2026 double-blind tocilizumab trial in difficult-to-treat depression with repeatedly elevated CRP. Thirty people were randomized and 29 received an infusion. The primary day-14 somatic outcome was null: adjusted difference −0.12, 95% CI −2.51 to 2.28. Later patterns favouring treatment justify further investigation, but do not establish efficacy. Small descriptive response and remission differences are especially unstable. Baseline CRP, not IL-6, tracked improvement.

Indirect intervention trials are mixed. A small celecoxib trial improved symptoms and lowered IL-6, while a pentoxifylline study reported changes in several cytokines, including lower IL-10. Conversely, zinc and probiotic studies reported selected clinical or cognitive benefits without IL-6 reductions. A larger ketamine biomarker analysis found no consistent relationship between inflammatory trajectories and improvement. These results separate treatment benefit from a claim that IL-6 suppression is its necessary mechanism.

Minocycline illustrates the uncertainty around inflammatory selection. The small CRP-enriched trial was negative overall, with exploratory signals in a higher-CRP subgroup; a separate 71-person trial analysis found no overall IL-6 change. The EPA dose-finding study also missed its prespecified IL-6 target and its clinical response comparisons were nonsignificant. These are research leads, not established biomarker-guided treatment rules.

Observational syntheses repeatedly associate depression with higher IL-6. Longitudinal studies suggest small relationships in both directions: inflammation can precede symptoms, and symptoms can precede inflammation. Fatigue, sleep, appetite and anhedonia do not all share identical associations. Genetic analyses support some IL-6-pathway hypotheses, while HUNT provides imprecise or discordant estimates. Metabolic, behavioural and immune mechanisms may overlap without being interchangeable.

A secondary hyperthermia analysis is a useful biological counterexample: a brief increase in the IL-6-to-soluble-receptor ratio related to later improvement. The authors interpret this as compatible with classical signalling, but the ratio is an indirect measure and the sample is small. This supports testing the timing and type of signalling rather than assuming that every IL-6 increase is harmful. A linked correction notice is retained in the source record.

topics.title: Schizophrenia and psychosis
topics.description: Peripheral and central associations; direct blockade remains unproven.
paragraphs: The double-blind schizophrenia tocilizumab trial randomized 36 adults and found no benefit on symptoms or cognition. CRP decreased while measured IL-6 increased. This is direct evidence that peripheral target engagement can occur without clinical improvement, and that receptor blockade is not the same as reducing the measured ligand concentration. The result does not settle every early-illness or inflammation-selected population, but it is central counterevidence.

The 207-person BeneMin trial also found no benefit of minocycline on negative symptoms or plasma IL-6 over 12 months, constraining smaller positive trials. Berberine produced positive findings in an open-label study with substantial attrition and per-protocol analysis. The small inflammation-enriched canakinumab trial targeted IL-1β, with strong CRP changes but limited clinical evidence. None establishes an OXTR-to-IL-6-to-recovery pathway.

Associations are more consistent than therapeutic results. Medication-naive first-episode studies show IL-6 elevations, reducing the likelihood that antipsychotics explain the entire association. Larger syntheses report elevations in both acute and chronic illness, while earlier reviews found greater state dependence. A CSF meta-analysis also found elevated IL-6, but blood and CSF evidence remain separate and neither measures all brain-cell signalling.

Clinical-risk groups show a small pooled IL-6 elevation, yet IL-6 did not reliably distinguish future converters from non-converters. Nor does distributional evidence consistently identify a discrete inflammatory subgroup. Stratifying a trial by repeated inflammation measurements is a testable research strategy, not an established biological subtype or a diagnostic tool. Genetic receptor associations add a different evidence layer with their own assumptions.

topics.title: Bipolar depression and euthymia
topics.description: Mood states, medication and biomarker change require separate interpretation.
paragraphs: Bipolar depression has several randomized biomarker studies, with mixed or negative clinical results. Pentoxifylline reduced inflammatory markers but did not beat placebo overall. Memantine added to valproate changed TNF but not IL-6 or clinical outcomes between groups. NAC-related analyses likewise did not demonstrate an overall IL-6 reduction. A cytokine response is not automatically a mood response.

The adaptive aspirin/minocycline trial reported response-rate and subgroup signals, while mean depression-score change had no significant main drug effect. Interim design and outcome changes, small cells and exploratory interactions limit certainty. In a separate bipolar II trial analysis, both treatment groups improved while quetiapine plus psychotherapy increased IL-6 relative to psychotherapy plus placebo. This directly challenges a simple model of recovery requiring lower IL-6.

Meta-analyses differ on whether IL-6 is predominantly a state or trait marker. The 2021 synthesis found elevations in depressed, manic and euthymic groups, whereas earlier work found less consistent depressed-state differences and no single marker that reliably separated phases. Most comparisons remain between people rather than repeated measurements through all states in the same person.

Euthymia is not absence of all biological change, yet peripheral and central findings can disagree. A small CSF study found lower IL-6 despite higher IL-1β, while another euthymic study found no difference in soluble IL-6 receptor. Receptor concentration, CSF cytokines and blood cytokines are distinct measurements. Medication, adiposity, sleep and recent episode history remain important covariates.

topics.title: Mania: state-sensitive and heterogeneous
topics.description: Positive findings coexist with smaller opposite-direction studies.
paragraphs: Some phase-comparison studies show elevated IL-6 during mania, with less consistent differences during remission. A longitudinal rapid-cycling study found higher IL-6 and IL-18 in manic/hypomanic states than depressed or euthymic states after adjustment. Repeated within-person sampling is particularly useful for testing whether inflammation tracks an episode.

An earlier small unmedicated study reported a contrasting manic pattern with lower IL-6 relative to depression. Sample size, episode definition, medication exposure, sleep loss, agitation, smoking and metabolic health can change the observed pattern. The evidence supports heterogeneity rather than an invariant mania marker.

A decisive next step is to distinguish onset, peak illness, treatment and recovery within the same participants, with prespecified clinical and immune endpoints. Existing associations do not establish selective IL-6 blockade as a treatment for mania, nor demonstrate that an OXTR-based intervention prevents or resolves manic episodes.

topics.title: Hypomania: a specific evidence gap
topics.description: Do not substitute bipolar depression or pooled mania findings for hypomania.
paragraphs: The clearest dedicated longitudinal lead links higher childhood IL-6 with hypomanic features at age 22 in ALSPAC. The adjusted top-versus-bottom-third odds ratio was 1.77, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.10–2.85. The association persisted after adjustment for depression at 18, but the outcome was a self-report hypomania checklist rather than confirmed bipolar disorder.

The rapid-cycling study pooled mania and hypomania. It therefore cannot establish a separate hypomania effect size. Bipolar II depression trials study a depressive episode, not the efficacy of IL-6 modulation during hypomania. These distinctions remain visible even when they leave a smaller evidence base.

No convincing hypomania-specific IL-6 intervention result was identified in this targeted set. A useful hypothesis is that a subset of episode transitions involves immune change, but prospective replication, precise episode ascertainment and attention to sleep and medication are needed before any clinical inference.

topics.title: Anxiety disorders: GAD, panic and social anxiety
topics.description: Diagnosis-specific positive and null findings.
paragraphs: Anxiety is not one inflammatory phenotype. In a large NESDA analysis, current anxiety disorders did not show an overall adjusted IL-6 association; social phobia sometimes showed lower values. Panic-disorder meta-analyses report higher IL-6 but with considerable heterogeneity. A broad anxiety-related meta-analysis found that PTSD largely drove the pooled inflammatory result.

The GAD psychotherapy RCT is especially instructive: symptoms improved, but the inflammatory profile did not improve as predicted, and IL-6 increased in the acceptance-based arm. An uncontrolled SSRI cohort showed falling IL-6 and anxiety, but lacks the randomized comparator needed to isolate a medication effect. These designs answer different questions.

A social-anxiety study found altered kynurenine metabolism and lower IL-10, without differences in basal or stimulated pro-inflammatory cytokines. Regulatory and metabolic pathways may matter even when IL-6 is not elevated. There is no validated general anxiety IL-6 threshold or established anxiety treatment based on selective IL-6 suppression in this set.

topics.title: PTSD and trauma
topics.description: Trauma exposure, disorder, stress reactivity and recovery are distinct.
paragraphs: Across meta-analyses, PTSD is associated with higher peripheral IL-6 on average. Effect sizes vary considerably. Whether controls have also experienced trauma matters: some subgroup analyses weaken or remove the difference, while other syntheses retain it. Depression comorbidity, medication, sex, assay and sampling time also affect estimates. Trauma exposure alone is not a PTSD diagnosis.

Small double-blind cervical vagus-stimulation experiments blocked IL-6 responses to traumatic scripts; a related 20-person pilot also reported symptom improvement. The acute study included only ten people with PTSD, and related reports belong to one research programme rather than multiple independent replications. These device results do not demonstrate oxytocin or OXTR mediation and cannot be transferred directly to music, social interaction or another intervention.

Pooled veteran mindfulness trials found no treatment-group difference in IL-6 change, despite clinical improvement. Small stress-challenge cohorts report potential predictive value for IL-6 and IL-10, but samples are too small to establish clinical selection rules. Resting concentration, stress reactivity and recovery kinetics remain different candidate endpoints.

Trauma-related distress can interact with sleep, metabolic health and behaviour over years. In the Nurses’ Health study analysis, IL-6 associations were clearer cross-sectionally, while the longitudinal signal centred on CRP. The separate DOCK2 chapter remains an exploratory epigenetic research strand; DOCK2, DOC2 and CK2 are different entities, and none establishes the proposed OXTR–IL-6 mechanism in PTSD.

topics.title: Suicidal ideation and behaviour
topics.description: Association does not establish individual prediction or prevention.
paragraphs: Suicidal ideation, attempts and death by suicide are distinct outcomes. Meta-analyses often find higher IL-6 against healthy controls, with smaller or absent differences against psychiatric controls. The 2025 depression-specific synthesis found no significant IL-6 difference between depressed people with and without suicidal behaviour, with extreme heterogeneity. This prevents treating a general depression association as suicide-specific biology.

In veterans, IL-6 tracked ideation severity but did not predict whether ideation was present. NESDA findings differed between ideation alone and attempt history. In psychosis, IL-2 and IL-10 carried the principal longitudinal associations rather than IL-6. Several case-control studies also found null or confounder-sensitive IL-6 results.

Specimen and timing can reverse interpretation. One synthesis reported serum/CSF elevations but lower plasma IL-6, with a numerical inconsistency in its abstract that is flagged in the register. Recent injury, infection, acute stress, toxic exposure and postmortem processes can influence cytokines around an attempt or death. Such measurements are not automatically premorbid risk markers.

Genetic evidence linking IL-6 signalling to a suicidality symptom is a mechanistic lead, not proof that IL-6 blockade prevents suicide. No clinical suicide-prediction test or prevention claim is made here. Future intervention research needs direct clinical outcomes and appropriate clinical oversight rather than substituting a blood-marker change for reduced risk.

topics.title: ADHD: a mixed and developing literature
topics.description: Paediatric findings, adult null results and intervention limits.
paragraphs: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition. Its IL-6 literature is smaller and less consistent than the depression or psychosis literature. A 2021 synthesis found no significant IL-6 difference; a 2022 synthesis found an elevation that lost significance when individual studies were removed. A 2026 network meta-analysis highlighted elevated IL-6 for autism, while ADHD findings centred on other markers. Autism results are not ADHD results.

The randomized evidence also conflicts. An older omega-3 trial reported reduced IL-6 and improved parent ratings. Vitamin D did not reduce IL-6 relative to placebo. In a probiotic pilot, IL-6 decreased in both arms, so that change was not specific to the probiotic. None establishes IL-6 as a routine ADHD treatment target or demonstrates an OXTR mechanism.

Some child and adolescent case-control studies show higher IL-6, sometimes without a relationship to symptom severity. An unmedicated adult study found no case-control IL-6 difference. Small samples, age, asthma, obesity, sleep, medication and comorbid behavioural conditions may contribute to disagreement. Cytokine findings from childhood cannot automatically be generalized to adults.

Prospective pregnancy and childhood-sleep studies offer developmental hypotheses. The maternal study used a multi-cytokine composite, so its effect cannot be attributed solely to IL-6. ALSPAC reported statistical mediation between early sleep problems and probable ADHD, but observational mediation is not a causal experiment. A prevention or treatment claim remains premature.

topics.title: Alcohol use disorder
topics.description: Exposure, withdrawal and recovery produce different immune patterns.
paragraphs: The 102-person, double-masked ibudilast trial found no benefit on heavy drinking and no peripheral inflammatory-marker effect. Its earlier two-week biomarker trial produced selected, often nominal signals; those findings did not establish a specific IL-6 mechanism and did not replicate as overall efficacy in the larger trial. Exenatide also failed to change inflammatory biomarkers in a post hoc AUD trial analysis.

The alcohol-specific meta-analysis found moderately higher IL-6, while thirteen other cytokines were not significantly different. A study excluding liver disease also reported elevated IL-6, showing that liver pathology is not the only possible explanation. Nonetheless, active drinking, withdrawal duration, nutrition, infection, smoking, adiposity and liver health all need attention in an individual study.

Lower is not always better: blunted IL-6 stress responses predicted more subsequent drinking in one alcohol-dependent cohort. Cue experiments in binge drinkers linked greater IL-6 reactivity to craving and later consumption, but did not test a treatment for diagnosed AUD. In a CBM trial, IL-6 was below assay detection and was unavailable for analysis; that is an assay limit, not proof of zero inflammation.

The systems-biology hypothesis therefore concerns dysregulated timing and coordination, not a single universally high cytokine. Clinical recovery, sustained drinking outcomes and functioning remain primary questions. An OXTR-based intervention can be investigated as a separate hypothesis, with no current evidence that its IL-6 effect treats AUD.

topics.title: Opioid use disorder
topics.description: Treatment cohorts and small intervention studies.
paragraphs: Memantine and dextromethorphan adjunct trials during methadone treatment reported selected treatment and immune findings, mainly involving TNF or regulatory markers. They did not establish a selective IL-6 mechanism. A very small sham-controlled tDCS study improved impulsivity but did not significantly reduce IL-6. A double-blind label is recorded separately from confirmation of random allocation.

Prospective cohorts associate higher IL-6 with poorer methadone-treatment outcomes and poorer memory or executive performance. Continued opioid exposure can also drive inflammatory change, creating reverse causation. Attrition was substantial in some studies, and related regional cohorts may overlap. These findings support investigation, not a validated relapse predictor.

Methadone-dose correlations do not establish that methadone causes inflammation: dose reflects clinical need and prior exposure. Infection, injection-related injury, pain, smoking, other substances and social conditions may confound comparisons. Effective addiction treatment and an experimental cytokine hypothesis are separate clinical questions.

topics.title: Stimulant use disorders: cocaine and methamphetamine
topics.description: Inflammatory signals are neither uniform nor synonymous with relapse reduction.
paragraphs: An exploratory CBD analysis in cocaine use disorder reported lower IL-6, but a biomarker result alone does not demonstrate abstinence or relapse prevention. A small ibudilast methamphetamine challenge study attenuated selected inflammatory measures; its positive treatment findings did not establish suppression of the later IL-6 response.

Methamphetamine case-control findings conflict: one study found higher IL-6 and associations with depressive symptoms, while another found no IL-6 difference despite oxidative and blood-cell abnormalities. Cocaine withdrawal studies also distinguish stimulated immune-cell secretion from resting blood concentrations. Substances, withdrawal stage and laboratory methods all matter.

A randomized contingency-management study provides another counterexample: the group with the largest cocaine-use reduction showed increased IL-6 and decreased IL-10. Immune recovery can involve changed responsiveness rather than monotonic cytokine suppression. This makes functional outcomes and repeated measures more informative than a single desired biomarker direction.

topics.title: Cannabis and nicotine: contextual evidence and gaps
topics.description: Exposure studies are not trials of diagnosed use disorders.
paragraphs: The two contextual papers retained here concern cannabis exposure in people with and without HIV, and cigarette smoking in older adults. Neither establishes IL-6 as a causal pathway in cannabis-use disorder or nicotine dependence. These papers are excluded from the 117 directly relevant mental-health count. The third contextual paper is the binge-drinking cue experiment.

The cannabis study’s main associations involved other inflammatory markers and composites, not a demonstrated IL-6 treatment effect. HIV and compartment-specific biology limit transfer to other populations. It provides no basis for claiming cannabis treats inflammation-related mental illness.

Smoking was associated with a mixed immune profile, including higher CRP and lower soluble IL-6 receptor. Tobacco exposure is therefore an important confounder in psychiatric cytokine studies. Nicotine, combustion products, smoking behaviour and dependence are distinct exposures; this targeted review leaves disorder-specific intervention gaps explicit.

topics.title: From OXTR to mental-health outcomes: a testable hypothesis
topics.description: Separate each link in the proposed causal chain.
paragraphs: A plausible systems model connects a defined intervention to OXTR-related signalling, immune regulation, neural or behavioural change, and meaningful clinical outcomes. The existing cell and animal OXTR literature supports selected links. The mental-health literature supports IL-6 associations and some pathway hypotheses. Combining those literatures creates a research hypothesis; it does not complete the causal chain in humans.

IL-6 can signal through membrane-bound IL-6 receptor and gp130, or through soluble-receptor complexes acting on gp130-expressing cells. Soluble gp130 provides important regulation of trans-signalling. Receptor blockade, lower ligand concentration, altered receptor shedding and altered cell responsiveness are different perturbations. Human IL-6 administration can also raise IL-10 and IL-1RA, demonstrating that pro-inflammatory and regulatory responses are linked.

For Universal Mind, a defensible question is whether a precisely defined intervention changes repeated IL-6-related measures and clinical outcomes, and whether OXTR-related biology contributes. Use a suitable comparator, prespecified outcomes, realistic masking, repeated baseline samples and a prespecified analysis of inflammation-related variation. Measure clinical benefit separately from biomarkers; a mediation analysis needs appropriate timing and assumptions and remains weaker than direct pathway perturbation.

A practical exploratory panel can include IL-6, hs-CRP, TNF, IL-1β, IL-10 and IL-1RA, with sIL-6R and soluble gp130 when the signalling question justifies them. Record detection limits, specimen type, collection time, recent infection, BMI, smoking, sleep, medication and substance exposure. IL-10 is regulatory, CRP is an acute-phase marker, and neither has a universally desirable direction. Lower IL6 RNA, lower circulating protein and lower pathway activity are not interchangeable endpoints.

Measure OXTR-related endpoints with cell-type and assay specificity. Plasma oxytocin, OXTR methylation and receptor expression do not prove receptor activation in the brain. No included paper validates the combined Universal Mind intervention–OXTR–IL-6–mental-health-benefit chain. The opportunity is a focused, transparent human research programme; any claim of global novelty needs a separate, protocol-specific search.

topics.title: Review method, quality and remaining gaps
topics.description: Transparent source counts, access depth and limits.
paragraphs: Searches and identifier checks were conducted on 28 November 2026 using public PubMed/Europe PMC records, publisher pages and accessible full text, with trial-first, diagnosis-specific and contradictory-result searches. The register contains 120 unique peer-reviewed publications, including 117 directly relevant mental-health papers and three contextual exposure papers. Protocols, registry entries, preprints and correction notices are not counted as new publications in this expansion.

This is a structured narrative evidence map, not a registered systematic review, an exhaustive database search, an individual-participant meta-analysis or a formal GRADE assessment. Searches were bounded and selection was purposive. All included abstracts were appraised; selected available full-text methods and results were checked for pivotal trials. Each record states access depth. Linked correction notices remain attached, with unresolved correction content explicitly flagged.

Nature-family, Frontiers and other specialist journals are represented, together with veteran and Navy-associated research. PubMed/NIH indexing and a government domain aid traceability; they do not guarantee low bias. Sample size, randomization, masking, outcome prespecification, attrition, comparator, confounding, multiplicity and replication carry more weight than a publisher or domain name. Publication Trust Factor is study-design shorthand, not a clinical-efficacy or certainty grade.

The companion register retains original identifiers, individual findings, limitations, trial/cohort-family links and bibliographic provenance. Reviews overlap primary studies. Where cohort independence, masking or a correction cannot be resolved, uncertainty remains visible. The website-wide JSON/CSV snapshots and Universal One use the same appraised records. Updating Universal One means versioned retrieval knowledge; it does not mean that model weights were fine-tuned.
